claim: The model uses only two variables: the identity of the loop and the phase along it.
source: The model uses only two variables: the identity of the loop and the phase along it.

claim: Current values of macroscopic variables predict future neuronal activity.

source: During backwards locomotion, RIML activation differs significantly between animals (p-value < 0.001, Materials and methods).

source: Yet, during a different behavior – dorsal turn – RIML activation is consistent across individuals (p-value ≈ 0.1), Materials and methods.

claim: For most neurons involved in locomotion, activity differs from animal to animal during execution of at least one type of locomotor behavior.
source: For most neurons involved in locomotion activity differs from animal to animal during execution of at least one type of locomotor behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Only three neurons were consistent in all behaviors.
source: Only three neurons were consistent in all behaviors.

claim: AVB and RID were the only locomotion-associated neurons whose activity failed to exhibit statistically significant differences among individual animals in any locomotor behavior.
source: AVB and RID were the only locomotion-associated (White et al., 1986; Lim et al., 2016) neurons whose activity failed to exhibit statistically significant differences among individual animals in any locomotor behavior.

source: Using this strategy, we reliably decoded the onset of backwards locomotion based on ∼100 neurons recorded in each animal individually (p-value < 0.001 relative to shuffle control, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a specific p-value.

claim: The ability to decode did not degrade appreciably when just 15 neurons identified in each animal were used (p-value approximately 0.5 within animal - all neurons vs. within animal - 15 neurons).
source: The ability to decode did not degrade appreciably when just 15 neurons identified in each animal were used (p-value ≈ 0.5 within animal - all neurons vs. within animal - 15 neurons, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a specific p-value.

claim: When activity from four animals was used to decode the 5th (leave one out) the correct decoding rate was indistinguishable from chance (p-value approximately 0.3).
source: Yet, activity from one animal cannot be used to reliably decode the onset of backing behavior in another animal. When activity from four animals was used to decode the 5th (leave one out) the correct decoding rate was indistinguishable from chance (p-value ≈ 0.3, Materials and methods) (Figure 1E).

claim: Mutual information between neuronal activity and behavioral state is degraded when neuronal activity is averaged among genetically identical individuals during locomotion in a simple environment.
source: Thus, mutual information between neuronal activity and behavioral state is degraded when neuronal activity is averaged among genetically identical individuals during locomotion in a simple environment.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the decoding analysis.

claim: All 302 neurons in C. elegans and all their connections are known.
source: All 302 neurons (White et al., 1986) in C. elegans and all their connections are known (Izquierdo and Beer, 2013; Bargmann and Marder, 2013; Varshney et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Simultaneous recordings of the majority of the neurons in the brain (head ganglia) of C. elegans have been performed in vivo using calcium imaging.
source: Simultaneous recordings of the majority of the neurons in the brain (head ganglia) of C. elegans have been performed in vivo using calcium imaging (Kato et al., 2015; Nguyen et al., 2016; Prevedel et al., 2014; Tian et al., 2009) (Figure 1A, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The graded activity of most C. elegans neurons make them better suited for calcium imaging compared to vertebrate nervous systems.
source: The graded activity of most C. elegans neurons (see Liu et al., 2018, however) make them better suited for calcium imaging compared to vertebrate nervous systems in which the utility of calcium imaging is limited by the slow speed of calcium indicators relative to the temporal precision of spike trains (Rad et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Biomechanics of locomotion of C. elegans are well-described by just a few movement modes.
source: Biomechanics of locomotion of C. elegans are well-described by just a few movement modes (Stephens et al., 2008) suggesting that the dynamics of the nervous system that controls locomotion are likely to be simple enough to be inferred from relatively short recordings of neuronal activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citation to Stephens et al. (2008).

claim: Locomotor behaviors fall into well-characterized individual distinct stereotyped behavioral subtypes.
source: Locomotor behaviors fall into well-characterized individual distinct stereotyped behavioral subtypes (Kato et al., 2015; Li et al., 2014; Luo et al., 2014; Larsch et al., 2013) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Neurons can be individually identified in different genetically identical C. elegans animals.
source: The final fundamental advantage of C. elegans as a model organism is that neurons can be individually identified in different genetically identical animals (Kato et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citation to Kato et al. (2015).

claim: The simulated and observed spectra are in good agreement for all frequencies above 0.05 Hz.
source: With the exception of the very low frequencies (<0.05 Hz) most strongly affected by the finite dataset effects, the spectra of all simulated neurons are statistically indistinguishable from experimentally observed neuronal activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The experimentally observed and de novo simulated distributions of dwell times in different behavioral states are in excellent agreement.
source: The experimentally observed and de novo simulated distributions of dwell times in different behavioral states are in excellent agreement (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: The model of the dynamics was constructed by estimating probability of transition between two states on the time scale of one time step dictated by data acquisition and GCAMP kinetics (approximately 1/3 of a second).
source: This is remarkable because the model of the dynamics was constructed by estimating probability of transition between two states on the time scale of one time step dictated by data acquisition and GCAMP kinetics (∼ 1/3 of a second).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The simulation reproduces the dynamics on the time scale longer than 100 s.
source: Yet, the simulation reproduces the dynamics on the time scale longer than 100 s.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: It has been argued that switching between different modes of locomotion in C. elegans is stochastic.
source: Based on the observations of abrupt stereotyped transitions in activity of many neurons (e.g. Figure 1A) and dwell times of locomotor behaviors, it has been argued that switching between different modes of locomotion in C. elegans is stochastic (Roberts et al., 2016; Srivastava et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

source: To test this prediction, we make use of a new dataset of calcium imaging in C. elegans from Nichols et al. (2017) (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and references the Nichols et al. (2017) study.

source: We restricted our analysis to the prelethargus N2 animals (n = 11) that were subjected to similar experimental conditions and imaging to those from Kato et al. (2015) dataset.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: No data from the Nichols et al. dataset was used for the construction of the model.
source: Critically, no data from the Nichols et al. dataset was used for the construction of the model.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

source: Animals in the dataset (Nichols et al., 2017) shared between 8 and 13 neurons with the neurons recorded by Kato et al. (2015) on the basis of which the neuronal dynamics model was constructed (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: For most phase bins, the expected time of simulated behavioral switch was indistinguishable from experimentally observed switch in motor command.
source: For most phase bins, the expected time of simulated behavioral switch was indistinguishable from experimentally observed switch in motor command.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Predictions made by the null model based solely on behavioral dwell time distributions deviate significantly from the timing of observed transitions.
source: In contrast, the predictions made by the null model based solely on behavioral dwell time distributions deviate significantly from the timing of observed transitions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Simulation-based predictions were strongly correlated with observed timing of behavioral transitions (correlation coefficient 0.74).
source: Consistent with observations in (Figure 3A) simulation-based predictions (filled circles) were strongly correlated with observed timing of behavioral transitions (correlation coefficient 0.74) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a specific correlation coefficient and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Predictions based solely on the dwell time distributions were less well correlated (p < 0.0001) with experimental observations.
source: In contrast, predictions based solely on the dwell time distributions were less well correlated (p < 0.0001) with experimental observations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a specific p-value and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The dispersion around the best fit line is smaller for the simulation-based than for dwell-time based predictions.
source: Further, note that the dispersion around the best fit line is smaller for the simulation-based than for dwell-time based predictions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Dynamics-based predictions are more precise and accurate than those based on behavioral statistics alone.
source: Thus, dynamics-based predictions are more precise and accurate than those based on behavioral statistics alone.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the analysis in Figure 3.

claim: The modeling approach reveals a strong contribution of deterministic dynamics to abrupt changes in locomotor direction in C. elegans.
source: Therefore, our modeling approach reveals a strong contribution of deterministic dynamics to abrupt changes in locomotor direction in C. elegans.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: The predictions do not depend strongly on activity of AVA–the command neuron for backward locomotion.
source: These predictions do not depend strongly on activity of AVA–the command neuron for backward locomotion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Knowing the initial conditions is sufficient to predict the expected time of transitions between different modes of locomotion 30 s before they are experimentally observed.
source: Knowing the initial conditions is sufficient to predict the expected time of transitions between different modes of locomotion 30 s before they are experimentally observed (Figure 3).

claim: These predictions are valid across individuals observed years apart.
source: Remarkably, these predictions are valid across individuals observed years apart.

source: Therefore, neuronal dynamics model can be applied universally across individuals despite significant inter-individual differences in neuronal activation and undersampling of neuronal activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the analysis.

source: Models built on some neurons involved in backwards locomotion (e.g. AVAL, AVAR, AVER, and RIML) yielded predictions comparable to those obtained for a set of 15 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Models based solely on RIML were approximately 75% as informative as models built upon the entire 15 neuron set.
source: Interestingly, although RIML is known to play a role in backward locomotion, its activity varied significantly among individual animals (Figure 1C) during backwards locomotion. Nevertheless, models based solely on RIML were ∼75% as informative as models built upon the entire 15 neuron set.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: At least in the simple nervous system of C. elegans a predictive model can be constructed on the basis of a single experimentally observed neuron as long as activation of this neuron is tightly coupled to the network that mediates the observed behaviors.
source: Thus, at least in the simple nervous system of C. elegans a predictive model can be constructed on the basis of a single experimentally observed neuron as long as activation of this neuron is tightly coupled to the network that mediates the observed behaviors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the single neuron analysis.

claim: The ability to simulate neuronal activity, behavioral dwell-time statistics, and even predict timing of individual behavioral transitions implies that trajectories traced by the state of the brain as it evolves in phase space are remarkably conserved among individuals.
source: The ability to simulate neuronal activity, behavioral dwell-time statistics, and even predict timing of individual behavioral transitions implies that trajectories traced by the state of the brain as it evolves in phase space are remarkably conserved among individuals.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the modeling results.

claim: The manifold in Figure 4A was constructed on the basis of all 107 neurons recorded in one animal.
source: The manifold in Figure 4A was constructed on the basis of all 107 neurons recorded in one animal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

source: This illustrates that our methodology is able to reconstruct the global dynamics in the limit of relatively large fraction (∼ 1/3) of all neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and can be applied to time series consisting of at least 100 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Although behavioral assignments were not used in the construction of the manifold, most regions of the manifold are associated with just one type of locomotor command.
source: Note that although behavioral assignments were not used in the construction of the manifold (Materials and methods), most regions of the manifold are associated with just one type of locomotor command.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Different locomotor commands are localized to different regions in the phase space.
source: In other words, different locomotor commands are localized to different regions in the phase space.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The manifold in Figure 4B was constructed on the basis of activity from all five animals using only 15 neurons identified in each animal.
source: The manifold in Figure 4B was constructed on the basis of activity from all five animals using only 15 neurons identified in each animal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Reconstruction of neuronal dynamics is possible even when only 15 neurons (approximately 5%) are consistently identified in each individual.
source: In contrast to averaging neuronal activity by applying PCA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) reconstruction of neuronal dynamics is possible even when only 15 neurons (∼5%) are consistently identified in each individual.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The structure of the manifold constructed on the basis of 15 neurons across individuals is nearly identical to the manifold constructed on the basis of 107 neurons in a single animal.
source: The structure of the manifold constructed on the basis of 15 neurons across individuals is nearly identical to the manifold constructed on the basis of 107 neurons in a single animal (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: The assigned behavioral state can be correctly decoded 83% of the time solely on the basis of position along the manifold in Figure 4B.
source: As a result, the assigned behavioral state can be correctly decoded 83% of the time solely on the basis of position along the manifold in Figure 4B.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Correct behavioral state assignment in the excluded animal can be decoded 81% of time (median correct decoding probability across all 426 manifold bins and all five animals left out in turn).
source: Behavioral states of the left out animal align well with the distribution of behavioral states along the manifold. Correct behavioral state assignment in the excluded animal can be decoded 81% of time (median correct decoding probability across all 426 manifold bins and all five animals left out in turn).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Averaging neuronal activity with respect to its position in phase space, rather than across individual neurons, preserves most of the behavioral information and can be universally applied across individuals even when only approximately 5% of neurons are uniquely identified.
source: Thus, averaging neuronal activity with respect to its position in phase space, rather than across individual neurons, preserves most of the behavioral information and can be universally applied across individuals even when only ∼5% of neurons are uniquely identified.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the manifold analysis.

claim: The conserved shape of the manifold in the phase space is what allows the predictions of timing of switching of motor commands across different animals.
source: This conserved shape of the manifold in the phase space is what allows the predictions of timing of switching of motor commands across different animals.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an explanation for the predictive power of the model.

claim: The manifold in C. elegans nervous system is composed of two loops.
source: The manifold in C. elegans nervous system is composed of two loops.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the region where the two loops merge, the behavior cannot be clearly predicted and stochastic forces play a stronger role.
source: While the system is in either one of the loops, its fate is largely predictable. Yet, in the neighborhood where the loops merge, the behavior cannot be clearly predicted and stochastic forces play a stronger role.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the manifold structure.

claim: The region where the two loops merge is a decision point where the nervous system is most susceptible to noise and/or sensory inputs.
source: This leads us to hypothesize that the region where the two loops merge is a decision point where the nervous system is most susceptible to noise and/or sensory inputs (Gordus et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on the manifold structure.

claim: Even in genetically identical organisms consistent differences in neuronal activity associated with motor commands are the norm.
source: Intriguingly, we find that even in genetically identical organisms consistent differences in neuronal activity associated with motor commands are the norm.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a key finding.

claim: Hodgkin-Huxley models of conductances measured in individual AB neurons in crustacean stomatogastric ganglion exhibit bursting akin to the biological neuron.
source: Hodgkin-Huxley models of conductances measured in individual AB neurons in crustacean stomatogastric ganglion exhibit bursting akin to the biological neuron.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citation to Golowasch et al. (2002).

claim: Averaging conductance measurements across AB neurons in different individuals yields models that fail to burst.
source: However, averaging conductance measurements across AB neurons in different individuals yields models that fail to burst (Golowasch et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citation to Golowasch et al. (2002).

claim: Virtually indistinguishable network activity patterns can arise from distinct biophysical mechanisms.
source: Virtually indistinguishable network activity patterns can arise from distinct biophysical mechanisms (Prinz et al., 2004; Chiel et al., 1999; Beer et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Differences between individual AB neurons or individual C. elegans are not simply random deviations from a common template that can be averaged away at the microscopic level.
source: This suggests that differences between individual AB neurons (Goldman et al., 2001; Prinz et al., 2004) or individual C. elegans are not simply random deviations from a common template that can be averaged away at the microscopic level.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Evolutionary selection operates at the macroscopic level of organismal behavior embodied by the global dynamics of the brain.
source: We hypothesize that the nontrivial degeneracy between microscopic biophysical processes and circuit-level dynamics arises because evolutionary selection operates at the macroscopic level of organismal behavior (Lässig and Valleriani, 2008) embodied by the global dynamics of the brain.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis supported by citation.

claim: There is no explicit selective pressure for each individual to produce identical neuronal activation during behavior.
source: Thus, there is no explicit selective pressure for each individual to produce identical neuronal activation during behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the evolutionary hypothesis.

claim: All that is required is that the overall system gives rise to an adaptive behavioral strategy.
source: All that is required is that the overall system gives rise to an adaptive behavioral strategy (Beer, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citation to Beer (2000).

claim: The biophysical details of neuronal circuits are constrained by the computation implemented by the circuit as a whole.
source: This is equivalent to David Marr's (Marr, 1982; Frégnac, 2017) proposal that the biophysical details of neuronal circuits are constrained by the computation implemented by the circuit as a whole, rather than the traditional bottom-up approach (Markram, 2006; Markram et al., 2015) which assumes the opposite.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to Marr and others.

claim: One should not necessarily expect a detailed model of the nervous system to be equally valid for different, seemingly identical, individuals.
source: Thus, one should not necessarily expect a detailed model of the nervous system to be equally valid for different, seemingly identical, individuals.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Kato et al. (2015) established some essential similarities between activation of neurons in the immobilized and freely moving C. elegans.
source: Although Kato et al. (2015) established some essential similarities between activation of neurons in the immobilized and freely moving C. elegans, there are also important differences (Nguyen et al., 2016; Venkatachalam et al., 2016; Scholz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: There are important differences between activation of neurons in the immobilized and freely moving C. elegans.
source: Although Kato et al. (2015) established some essential similarities between activation of neurons in the immobilized and freely moving C. elegans, there are also important differences (Nguyen et al., 2016; Venkatachalam et al., 2016; Scholz et al., 2018).
